To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scalar singlet dark matter candidate is excluded at 95% CL, while the Dirac singlets are not.
the isotropic diffuse γ-ray flux from the Galactic halo can be used to constrain light dark matter candidates.

the Fermi-LATT data on the isotopic gamma-ray diffuse emission can be used to exclude a light scalar dark matter candidate, MDM ~ GeV, with a spin-independent elastic scattering on nucleons σn0 ~ few×10−39cm2 and an annihilation cross section σann ~ few×10-26cm3s-1, while the same data are not able to constrain a similar Dirac singlet dark matter candidate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether light dark matter candidates can be excluded using the Fermi gamma-ray data.
the question of whether or not light dark matter candidates may be ruled out by the isotropic gamma ray background.
the possibility that the isotropic diffuse emission of gamma rays may help in the discrimination between different light dark matter candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the light WIMP scenario, the singlet scalar is excluded, while the Dirac singlets are not, at least not in their simplest form.
, although it is possible to set some constraints from the isotropic gamma-rays on light WIMP dark matter candidates, it is not possible to exclude the candidates considered here.

the Fermi-Lat data on the isotopic gamma-ray emission do not exclude the light dark matter candidates considered here, but they can be used to set constraints on the parameter space of the models, and to provide some motivation for further studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fermi-Lat data on the isotopic gamma-ray background excludes the scalar singlet candidate as a possible light dark matter candidate.
the isotropic gamma-rays diffuse emission data are not able to rule out light WIMP candidates.
, for the singlet scalar, the isotropic diffuse emission is a competitive probe, and for the Dirac fermion, it is complementary to other indirect detection probes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fermi-Lat data can be used to put constraints on light WIMP dark matter candidates, in particular on the singlet scalar.

, if the Fermi-Lat data on the isotopic diffuse gamma-ray emission are interpreted as being due to the annihilation of dark matter particles, then the singlet scalar is excluded, while the singlet Dirac fermion is not.
the Fermi-Lat data are competitive with direct detection experiments in constraining the parameter space of light dark matter candidates.
